adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrency test lacks start/join/latch synchronization, so it can pass without exercising the race (reader thread may never run, and exceptions after assertion are dropped)

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and controlled only by an `AtomicBoolean` flag. There is no start barrier/latch to ensure the reader actually runs during the delete loop, and there is no `join()`/latch to ensure it has stopped before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. As written, the test can trivially pass without exercising the intended concurrent read/delete race, and exceptions could be added after the assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test does not demonstrate the pre-fix failure (no full-representation read or direct getSubGroupsCount() call concurrent with deletion), so reverting the fix still passes

adjudication.rationale: The added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()` only loops on `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` (brief representation) while deleting groups. It never does a direct `getSubGroupsCount()` call nor any full-representation group read, so from the diff alone there is no clear linkage that this test exercises the changed logic in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (now null-checking `modelSupplier.get()`). Thus it may not fail pre-fix and may not validate the fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Leaked non-daemon reader thread with unbounded busy-loop can hang the JVM after test failure and starve the delete thread on slow CI

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, a non-daemon `new Thread(...).start()` is launched with a tight `while (!deletedAll.get())` loop and no sleep/backoff. The thread is never joined or otherwise guaranteed to stop if the test fails/throws before `deletedAll.set(true)` (e.g., during group creation or deletion), which can leak the thread and keep the JVM/test process alive. The unbounded busy-loop can also consume significant CPU during the test run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null-guard applied only to getSubGroupsCount(); other GroupAdapter methods delegating through getGroupModel()/modelSupplier.get() (getName, getParent, getSubGroupsStream, getAttributes, getRoleMappingsStream) still NPE under concurrent deletion race

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` was changed from `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to `modelSupplier.get()` with a null-check, implying `modelSupplier.get()` can be null (e.g., concurrent deletion). The finding’s broader claim that other delegating methods (e.g., `getName`, `getParent`, `getSubGroupsStream`, etc.) still NPE is plausible but not directly verifiable from the provided diff because those methods and `getGroupModel()`’s implementation are not shown. What is verifiable is the inconsistency/incompleteness: only this one method now guards against a null model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() returns null on missing model, which callers consume via unboxing/Long arithmetic, relocating the NPE to the caller with a less diagnostic stack trace and making an unauthorized silent-null contract change

adjudication.rationale: In GroupAdapter#getSubGroupsCount(), the diff changes behavior from always delegating to getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount() to `GroupModel model = modelSupplier.get(); return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`. This introduces a new possible `null` return for a “count” accessor, which is a silent contract change and can shift failures (e.g., NPE on unboxing/arithmetic) to callers rather than failing at the source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of private method groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement in GroupUtils.java is unrelated dead-code cleanup / scope drift smuggled into the concurrency-fix PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a private helper method `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` being removed from `GroupUtils.java` with no replacement or related changes in that file. Since it was `private`, this is a self-contained cleanup (likely unused dead code) and not directly tied to the concurrency/null-handling changes in `GroupAdapter` or the new concurrent test. That makes it a plausible scope-drift / unrelated-change concern, though intent can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding @Override to getRealm() in CachedGroup.java is an unrelated cosmetic change mixing compile-level churn into the concurrency fix

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only a single-line addition of `@Override` above `CachedGroup#getRealm()`, with no behavioral change. Calling it “unrelated cosmetic churn” is a subjective style/nit rather than a concrete, actionable review issue grounded in correctness or the concurrency fix shown elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test does not enforce the invariant: reader thread is never joined and the empty-exceptions assertion runs immediately, so the test passes vacuously and the NPE regression can re-emerge while the test stays green

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start();` but its reference is not kept and it is never `join()`ed. After deleting groups, the test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());`. Because the reader thread may still be running (or may not have had time to record exceptions) when the assertion executes, the test can pass even if exceptions occur shortly after, making it potentially vacuous and not reliably enforcing the intended invariant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test never exercises getSubGroupsCount (the only changed code path), leaving the changed line with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` and adds a new concurrency-focused admin API test (`createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`) that repeatedly calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)`. The test does not directly call `getSubGroupsCount()`, but from the diff alone we cannot verify whether that admin call internally exercises `getSubGroupsCount()` or whether other existing tests cover it. Also, the statement "the only changed code path" is incorrect because the diff includes other changes (e.g., `CachedGroup#getRealm()` annotation, removal of a helper in `GroupUtils`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test leaks resources and determinism: reader thread runs a tight unbounded loop with no sleep, timeout, interrupt, or join in finally, potentially spinning forever if the main thread fails

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a non-daemon `new Thread(...).start()` is created and never joined or interrupted. The reader thread runs a tight loop `while (!deletedAll.get()) { managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...); }` with no sleep/timeout/finally guard. If the main test path throws before `deletedAll.set(true)` (e.g., during create/delete), or if the groups call blocks, the thread can continue running and potentially keep the JVM/test suite alive or cause nondeterministic hangs/spin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() returns null as a sentinel for concurrently evicted groups, causing NPE at call sites that unbox the Long instead of fixing the failure; should re-fetch the live model instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getSubGroupsCount()` changed to return `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). However, the finding’s claim that this "caus[es] NPE at call sites that unbox the Long" and that it should "re-fetch the live model" is not verifiable from the provided diff (no call sites or unboxing behavior are shown). The change may be intentional to avoid NPEs during concurrent eviction/deletion, and the asserted downstream NPE is speculative here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The null guard is scoped only to getSubGroupsCount() while the check-then-use race against cache eviction exists in every GroupAdapter method that calls getGroupModel(), so the test can still fail intermittently

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a null-guard/race mitigation added only in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (switching from `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to `modelSupplier.get()` with a null check). The new concurrency test (`createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`) reads groups while deleting them, so if similar check-then-use patterns exist in other `GroupAdapter` methods (not shown in this diff), this change could be an incomplete fix and the test could still intermittently hit other code paths. However, the claim about "every GroupAdapter method" cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupTest never joins the reader thread, so the assert can execute before a late exception is caught, allowing the test to go green while the race was hit and leaking the thread into subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a reader thread is started via `new Thread(() -> { ... }).start();` without keeping a reference or calling `join()`. After deletions, `deletedAll.set(true);` is set and the test immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());`. The reader thread may still be running (and could catch an exception after the assert), and the thread can also outlive the test, leaking into subsequent tests. This can let the test pass despite a late exception and introduces nondeterminism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) is an unbounded full-realm read in a tight loop; a bounded window plus retry loop would amplify the race without unbounded materialization

adjudication.rationale: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` spins a background thread that repeatedly calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` in a `while (!deletedAll.get())` loop. This is an unbounded, full-realm read in a tight loop (no sleep/backoff, huge max), which can unnecessarily materialize large result sets and make the test slow/flaky or overly resource-intensive. It’s a test-quality/performance concern rather than a functional defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the backing model is concurrently deleted, causing NPE at caller sites that unbox the Long, only relocating the crash rather than fixing it

adjudication.rationale: In GroupAdapter#getSubGroupsCount the diff changes behavior from always delegating to getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount() to returning null when modelSupplier.get() returns null (likely on concurrent deletion): `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`. This introduces a new nullable return path for a “count” method. The finding’s specific claim that this will “cause NPE at caller sites that unbox the Long” is plausible, but the diff does not show any caller sites or unboxing, so the crash relocation cannot be directly verified from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null Long propagates into GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount or REST serialization, producing wrong or missing counts with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` from always delegating to `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to returning `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This introduces a new code path where a `Long` count becomes `null`, which can propagate to callers (e.g., representations/REST) and result in missing/incorrect subgroup counts or potential unboxing/serialization issues instead of failing loudly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Intent drift from 'prevent NPE' to 'tolerate null model' without an explicit decision about semantics; null return is an undocumented contract change to one implementation only

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, the code changes from unconditionally calling `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to `modelSupplier.get()` and returning `null` when the model is `null`. This is a real semantic change (from “will throw/NPE if model is absent” to “silently return null”), and it affects only this implementation in the diff. The diff does not show an explicit decision/documentation about the contract for `getSubGroupsCount()` or corresponding changes elsewhere, so the concern about undocumented behavior drift is grounded but not provably a concrete defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix is a single-method local patch: isUpdated() branch can still throw NPE if updated is null, and sibling methods like getSubGroupsStream still call getGroupModel() directly, so the same race reproduces elsewhere

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes `getSubGroupsCount()` to use `modelSupplier.get()` with a null check. It does not show the implementation of `isUpdated()` or whether `updated` can be null when `isUpdated()` is true, so the claimed NPE in the `isUpdated()` branch is not verifiable from the diff. Likewise, the diff does not show the bodies of sibling methods like `getSubGroupsStream()`, so the claim that they still call `getGroupModel()` directly cannot be confirmed from what’s shown.

This is an unrelated functional cleanup bundled with other changes, so reverting the main fix would also revert this separate deletion (scope creep concern).

From the diff alone, there is no evidence that the admin client would *not* throw on an HTTP 500 (i.e., that it would swallow a server error and return normally), so the claim that the test would still pass “even if the NPE regression returns” depends on external client behavior not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null where it previously threw NPE, and callers that unbox the Long (e.g., long count = adapter.getSubGroupsCount()) would just convert the NPE to a different location — a reliability/contract question

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() from always delegating (and potentially NPE’ing if underlying model is missing) to explicitly returning null when modelSupplier.get() returns null: `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`. This is a behavioral/contract change: callers may previously have seen an NPE inside getGroupModel()/getSubGroupsCount, but now could receive a null Long and hit an NPE when unboxing elsewhere. Whether that’s a defect depends on the expected nullability contract of getSubGroupsCount(), which isn’t verifiable from this diff alone, but it is a concrete reliability/API concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti can pass with zero concurrent reads because the reader thread is never joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, so it does not verify the NPE fix

adjudication.rationale: In GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start();` but it is never joined or otherwise synchronized before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());`. After deletions, the main thread sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts, so the test can finish before the reader thread performs any (or enough) `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` calls. This makes the test potentially non-deterministic and able to pass without actually exercising concurrent reads relevant to the NPE fix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No synchronization ensures the reader thread entered its loop before deletion finished, so on a fast machine the reader may perform 0 listing calls and the test trivially passes

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread is started (`new Thread(...).start();`) and the main thread immediately deletes all groups and sets `deletedAll` to true. There is no latch/barrier/join to ensure the reader loop actually runs at least once before `deletedAll` becomes true. On a fast run, the reader may observe `deletedAll` already true and perform zero `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` calls, making `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` trivially pass without exercising concurrent read/delete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The test uses briefRepresentation = true in the read path, which does not invoke getSubGroupsCount() on the adapter, so the fixed code branch is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the read loop calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation = true` (and even comments "just loading briefs"). The code change being fixed is in `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, but the diff does not show any assertion or API call in the test that would necessarily require `getSubGroupsCount()` to be evaluated; therefore the test may not exercise the newly added null-safe branch in `getSubGroupsCount()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The assertion can run before the reader thread terminates, allowing an exception to be thrown after the assertThat and pass unnoticed, and the leaked thread can crash unrelated tests later in the suite

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a reader `new Thread(...).start()` is launched but never joined or otherwise awaited. The test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately executes `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. Since the reader thread may still be running briefly after `deletedAll.set(true)`, it can add exceptions to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion, making the test falsely pass. Also, the unjoined thread can outlive the test and interfere with later tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null instead of throwing NPE when the cached group has been invalidated mid-request, altering in-memory read path behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` from `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to `modelSupplier.get()` with a null-guard returning `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change in the read path when the underlying model becomes unavailable (previously could throw NPE via dereference; now it returns null). Whether returning null is correct vs. preserving prior semantics is unclear from the diff alone, but it’s a notable contract/behavior change for callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMultiReadMulti fails to join the reader Thread before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, allowing exceptions after deletedAll.set(true) so the assert can pass while the reader thread is mid-request

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a reader `Thread` is started and loops until `deletedAll.get()` is true, collecting exceptions into `caughtExceptions`. After deleting groups, the test calls `deletedAll.set(true)` and immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, but it never `join()`s the reader thread (or otherwise waits for it to finish). This creates a race where the reader thread may still be mid-request or may catch and record an exception after the assertion, making the test potentially pass incorrectly and/or be flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Leaked non-daemon reader thread in the test can hang the test JVM, causing flaky false success on the race the test exists to catch

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the test starts a new `Thread` (`new Thread(() -> { while (!deletedAll.get()) { ... } }).start();`) that is not marked daemon, is not joined, and cannot be interrupted (no reference kept). Even though `deletedAll` is set to true at the end, the reader thread may be blocked inside `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` and never re-check the flag, leaving a live non-daemon thread that can keep the JVM running and make the test flaky/hang.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() returns null instead of fixing the concurrent-delete race, shifting the NPE to callers who unbox the Long

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, the diff changes behavior from always returning `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to potentially returning `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` is `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This introduces a new nullable return path in a count accessor that previously did not return null, which can break callers that assume a non-null `Long` (especially if unboxed to `long`).
